title: Telemetry-driven Setpoint Adaptor with Contracted Safety Limits
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a telemetry-driven setpoint adaptor for the Dedicated autoscaling policy engine that translates high-level throughput guarantees and tenant contracts into actionable scaling setpoints while enforcing safety limits and cost-aware throttles. The adaptor sits between the policy compiler and the scaling executor; responsibilities include: 1) selecting the active target metric (throughput, p95/p99 latency, token/successful-token rate, queue depth, KV cache hit-rate) per-tenant and per-route using configurable priority lists; 2) computing a short-term predictive setpoint using an ensemble of estimators (EWMA demand, AR(1) predictive warmup, and a headroom-credit model); 3) applying safety transforms (max scale rate, min idle capacity, surge quarantine, per-minute headroom budget, cost-budget throttle) and emitting the final setpoint and expiry; 4) recording decision provenance for rollbacks and explainability. Key design principles: prefer latency SLOs for low-concurrency, prefer throughput for batch workloads; conservative warmup when model weights are cold; explicit cost guard rails for free-tier vs committed customers. The adaptor must be deterministic for identical inputs and produce verbose explainability metadata for Console and incident postmortems.

Scope: 1) Setpoint selection and metric prioritization config API; 2) Predictive setpoint estimator library; 3) Safety transforms pipeline; 4) Explainability and telemetry hooks; 5) Unit/integration tests and a canary rollout plan for a single Dedicated fleet (dev-fleet-us-west). Not in scope: new autoscaler executor implementation (uses existing actuator), billing integration beyond cost budget signal, and per-tenant legal contract parsing.

Trade-offs considered: - Aggressive predictive scaling reduces p99 violations but increases cost and churn; selected approach uses tunable headroom credits to limit churn. - Using latency as primary target can oscillate for spiky short-lived tails; we add minimum stability windows and derivative damping. - Heavier telemetry models (AR) provide better predictions but are more resource-intensive; we default to EWMA + lightweight AR on fleets with >1k qps.

Deliverables: design doc (Confluence) link, adaptor library merged, feature-flagged rollout, metrics/dashboards, and post-rollout SLO impact report.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Telemetry+Setpoint+Adaptor PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8124 Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/autoscale/telemetry-setpoint-canary

Security: adaptor reads tenant-level config and cost-budget signal; access via RBAC-only service account. KMS keys used for reading sensitive contract IDs (integrated via runtime secrets).
acceptance_criteria: Adaptor produces setpoint decisions consistent with simulator baseline across 95% of synthetic workloads
Canary fleet (dev-fleet-us-west) shows <=10% increase in token-cost and >=50% reduction in p99 SLO violations for targeted routes
Explainability traces are emitted for every setpoint with decision keys and provenance, visible in Console rollout logs
Feature rolled out behind feature flag with instant rollback path and automated canary cutover test
Unit tests cover metric prioritization, safety transforms, and deterministic decision paths
